name: Logic and Formal Reasoning
description: Reasoning rigorously about programs and specifications: propositional and predicate logic, proof systems, Hoare logic and loop invariants, formal specification and an introduction to computability.

topics.name: Propositional Logic
topics.summary: The logic of whole statements — the foundation every later system builds on.

subtopics.name: Syntax and Semantics
subtopics.summary: Well-formed formulae, valuations, satisfiability and validity.

objectives.text: Distinguish a well-formed formula from a malformed one
Determine whether a formula is satisfiable, valid or unsatisfiable
Evaluate a formula under a given valuation

subtopics.name: Logical Equivalence and Laws
subtopics.summary: De Morgan, distribution, contraposition and the substitution of equals.

objectives.text: Prove two formulae equivalent using logical laws
Apply De Morgan's laws to push negation inwards
Simplify a formula to a minimal equivalent form

subtopics.name: Normal Forms
subtopics.summary: Conjunctive and disjunctive normal form, and why solvers want CNF.

objectives.text: Convert a formula to conjunctive normal form
Explain the role of CNF in automated satisfiability solving
State why conversion to CNF can blow up in size

topics.name: Predicate Logic
topics.summary: Quantifying over a domain — enough expressive power to state real specifications.

subtopics.name: Quantifiers and Binding
subtopics.summary: Universal and existential quantifiers, bound and free variables, and scope.

objectives.text: Identify free and bound occurrences of a variable
Translate an English specification into a quantified formula
Explain why quantifier order changes meaning

subtopics.name: Models and Interpretation
subtopics.summary: Domains, interpretations, and what makes a formula true in a structure.

objectives.text: Evaluate a quantified formula in a given finite model
Construct a model that satisfies a formula and one that falsifies it
Distinguish validity from truth in a particular model

subtopics.name: Formal Proof
subtopics.summary: Rules for introducing and eliminating quantifiers in a derivation.

objectives.text: Apply universal instantiation and existential generalisation correctly
Construct a short formal derivation from stated premises
Identify an invalid quantifier step in a proposed proof

topics.name: Proof Systems
topics.summary: Mechanising reasoning — what a proof system is, and what it can and cannot achieve.

subtopics.name: Natural Deduction
subtopics.summary: Introduction and elimination rules, assumptions and discharge.

objectives.text: Construct a natural deduction proof for a propositional entailment
Explain how an assumption is discharged by implication introduction
Identify the rule applied at each step of a given derivation

subtopics.name: Soundness and Completeness
subtopics.summary: The relationship between what is provable and what is true.

objectives.text: State what soundness and completeness each claim about a proof system
Explain why soundness is the property that makes a proof trustworthy
Describe the consequence of a proof system being incomplete

subtopics.name: Resolution and Automated Reasoning
subtopics.summary: Refutation, the resolution rule, and how automated provers search.

objectives.text: Apply the resolution rule to a pair of clauses
Prove a propositional entailment by refutation
Explain why automated provers work with clauses rather than arbitrary formulae

topics.name: Reasoning About Programs
topics.summary: Proving a program correct rather than testing it and hoping.

subtopics.name: Preconditions and Postconditions
subtopics.summary: Hoare triples, partial correctness, and specifying what code must achieve.

objectives.text: Write a Hoare triple specifying a fragment of code
Distinguish partial from total correctness
Determine whether a given triple holds for a short program

subtopics.name: Loop Invariants
subtopics.summary: The assertion that survives every iteration, and the variant that guarantees termination.

objectives.text: State a loop invariant that establishes a loop's postcondition
Verify that an invariant is preserved by the loop body
Give a variant expression that proves a loop terminates

subtopics.name: Weakest Preconditions
subtopics.summary: Working backwards from what must hold at the end to what must hold at the start.

objectives.text: Compute the weakest precondition of an assignment for a given postcondition
Derive the weakest precondition through a conditional statement
Use weakest preconditions to check a specification is satisfiable

topics.name: Formal Specification
topics.summary: Saying precisely what a component must do, before writing the code that does it.

subtopics.name: Specifying Behaviour
subtopics.summary: Writing unambiguous specifications and distinguishing them from implementations.

objectives.text: Write a formal specification for a described operation
Explain why a specification should not constrain implementation choices
Identify an ambiguity in an informal requirement

subtopics.name: Abstraction Functions and Representation Invariants
subtopics.summary: Relating concrete data structures to the abstract values they stand for.

objectives.text: State the representation invariant of a data structure implementation
Define an abstraction function from concrete state to abstract value
Show that an operation preserves the representation invariant

subtopics.name: Refinement
subtopics.summary: Replacing a specification with an implementation that is guaranteed to satisfy it.

objectives.text: Explain what it means for an implementation to refine a specification
Check whether a proposed refinement weakens the postcondition
Describe stepwise refinement as a development method

topics.name: Introduction to Computability
topics.summary: The limits of what any program can decide — a first look at problems with no algorithm.

subtopics.name: Decidability
subtopics.summary: Decision problems, decidable and undecidable languages, and what a decider is.

objectives.text: State what it means for a decision problem to be decidable
Give an example of a decidable and an undecidable problem
Distinguish a decider from a recogniser

subtopics.name: The Halting Problem
subtopics.summary: The classic undecidable problem and its diagonalisation argument.

objectives.text: State the halting problem precisely
Outline the contradiction that shows it is undecidable
Explain what its undecidability means for program analysis tools

subtopics.name: Reductions
subtopics.summary: Proving a new problem undecidable by transforming a known one into it.

objectives.text: Explain how a reduction transfers undecidability between problems
Set up a reduction from the halting problem to another problem
State the direction a reduction must run to prove undecidability
